title: [PD] Enable deferred decode-side KV release by default
body:
## Motivation

When a decode request is aborted while its prefill->decode KV transfer may still be in flight, the decode side frees the request's KV pages and metadata slot immediately. A prefill write that is still in flight can then land on pages that have already been handed to another request — silent KV corruption for the victim request.

The deferred release (added behind `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE`) fixes that: the decode holds the pages until every notified prefill rank acks that its transfer drained, or a timeout fires. It shipped off by default; this PR makes it the default so PD deployments get the correct behavior without an opt-in.

## Modifications

- `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE` now defaults to `True`. Set it to `False` to restore the immediate release. `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE_TIMEOUT` (30s) is unchanged and bounds the hold.
- Gate the env var on a per-backend opt-in, mirroring the existing `supports_role_switch` pattern: `BaseKVManager.supports_deferred_decode_kv_release = False`, set `True` on `MooncakeKVManager` (ascend inherits its bootstrap/transfer threads) and `NixlKVManager`. `CommonKVManager.__init__` ANDs the env var with it.

  This matters because the hold is only released early by the prefill's `ABORT_ACK`. Mori's bootstrap thread marks the aborted room Failed but never acks, so turning the flag on globally would make every abort-mid-transfer on mori wait out the full 30s timeout while holding pages. Mori (and the fake backend) keep the immediate release.
- Added unit tests for the opt-in: the env default is on, mooncake/nixl opt in, and a backend that does not ack stays opted out.

Version skew is safe in both directions: a decode running this change against an older prefill that sends the legacy 2-frame `ABORT_ACK` simply does not count the ack and falls back to the timeout; an older decode ignores the extra rank frame.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output changes — abort/teardown path only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No steady-state impact: the hold only engages on a decode-initiated abort of an in-flight transfer, and releases as soon as the prefill acks the drain.

title: [RL] Add RL weight-update sessions and support updating spec draft runners
body:
## Motivation

Port the sglang-miles weight-update core to main as its final state. On main the draft-runner handling in `SchedulerWeightUpdaterManager` guesses the runner layout through `getattr` chains, each weight path enumerates draft runners its own way (tensor through per-worker overrides, disk/IPC through `draft_runners`), `update_weights_from_distributed` never reaches the draft model, and a refit never re-runs `process_weights_after_loading`: `update_weights_from_{tensor,distributed}` only call `model.load_weights`, so any format whose postprocess changes layout (Marlin repack, MXFP8 shuffles, NVFP4 swizzles) is left in checkpoint layout under kernels that expect the processed one. Schemes whose kernel layout also changes parameter shapes (compressed-tensors W4A16 MoE on Marlin) additionally need a restore before the checkpoint-format values can be loaded.

## Modifications

- `begin_weight_update` / `end_weight_update` session RPCs (HTTP, `Engine`, `HttpServerEngineAdapter`, `TokenizerManager` under the pause-aware writer lock). `begin` restores in-place-packed weights to a loadable state; `end` finalizes quantized weights into kernel layout, and runs `post_load_weights` only when no weights were loaded through the engine during the session (P2P/RDMA writes). One session spans many buckets, so finalize runs once per refit.
- **One runner enumeration for every weight op.** `weight_update_runners()` returns `(role, ModelRunner)` pairs; the scheduler's `_select_runners(selector)` concatenates the target's and the draft's, and disk, IPC, tensor, distributed, check and begin/end all iterate it. The worker-level `update_weights_from_*` methods on `BaseTpWorker`, `BaseSpecWorker`, `EAGLEWorkerV2`, `NGRAMWorker` and `UnoWorkerV2` are removed.
  - `BaseSpecWorker.weight_update_runners()` derives from `draft_worker.draft_runners` (#31078), so EAGLE, Standalone and FrozenKV MTP need no override. It is defined on the base rather than abstract: DFlash, DSpark and UNO forward unknown attributes to the target worker via `__getattr__`, so a missing method would silently re-enumerate the target runner.
  - Overrides only where `draft_runners` cannot express the family: multi-layer EAGLE (one `draft_step_{i}` role per step), DFlash and DSpark (draft worker is a plain `TpModelWorker`; DSpark only on the last PP stage). NGRAM and UNO have no draft worker and return `[]`.
  - `_draft_model_runners()` is untouched: it enumerates runners with their own KV pool (hicache), and FrozenKV MTP is deliberately absent there while it does own weights.
- A `{target, draft, all}` selector on tensor, distributed, check and begin replaces `disable_draft_model`. Role `"target"` is unprefixed in checksum keys; draft roles are prefixed.
- `update_weights_from_distributed` receives once on the target runner and loads into each selected runner; draft runners never join the update group.
- `check_weights` merges per-role payloads; `ChecksumInfo` carries one `parallelism_info` entry per role plus an optional `skip_tensor_list`. `role` is a field of the pydantic `ParallelismInfo` in `weight_checker` (the wire struct mirrors it), passed per runner from the scheduler.
- `update_weights_from_{tensor,distributed}` require an open session; calls outside one, a nested `begin`, or an `end` without `begin` return `success=False` (HTTP 400) rather than raising in the scheduler, which would SIGQUIT the server. In-repo callers, tests and `docs/advanced_features/sglang_for_rl.mdx` (new "Weight Update Session" section) are updated.
- Session restore/finalize live on the runner's `WeightUpdater` (`model_runner.py` stays orchestration-only), and every load goes through `WeightUpdater`, keeping the weight-cache and derived-weight-cache guards. The finalize reuses `DefaultModelLoader.postprocess_weights` (#34981) instead of a second copy of the per-module loop, and `restore_weights_before_loading` sits beside it as a staticmethod. The shared module walk skips LoRA wrappers: `FusedMoEWithLoRA` forwards `quant_method` but owns no expert params, so on main `update_weights_from_disk` on a MoE-LoRA model with quantized experts calls `process_weights_after_loading` on the wrapper and raises `AttributeError`. Startup loads run before LoRA wraps the model, so the skip is a no-op there.

Squash of sglang-miles #28001, #28575, #27750, #18565, #29675, #22663 plus the rebase fixups; the later commits are the cleanup pass and the enumeration unification.

### Disk/IPC behavior vs main, per family

- **Target**: `TpModelWorker.update_weights_from_{disk,ipc}` was a one-line forward to `model_runner.weight_updater`; the scheduler now calls the runner directly with the same arguments.
- **EAGLE / Standalone / FrozenKV MTP / multi-layer EAGLE**: same runners as `BaseSpecWorker`'s loop over `draft_runners`, same order (target first), same arguments.
- **UNO**: its disk/IPC methods were no-ops; it now contributes no runners.
- **NGRAM / DFlash / DSpark**: previously `AttributeError` (no `draft_runners` on their draft worker). NGRAM now updates the target only. **DFlash and DSpark gain disk/IPC updates** of their draft runner.
- Cache flush and version recording keep main's semantics: flush once the target runner loaded even if a draft runner fails afterwards; record the version only if every runner succeeded.

## Not supported by this PR

- `CompressedTensorsWNA16TritonMoE` (the SM100 auto default for W4A16 MoE) cannot be refit: its postprocess rebinds the packed params to new uint8 `Parameter`s behind a one-shot `is_triton_converted` flag, so the next load fails on shape (`RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (2048) must match the size of tensor b (1024)`, reproduced on B200 with the test above switched to `--moe-runner-backend triton`). Pin `marlin` for W4A16 RL on Blackwell until that is fixed.
- Formats whose postprocess is not re-runnable after a full reload (MXFP4, compressed-tensors W4A16 linear layers, per-tensor FP8 linear) are not made refit-safe here.

## Breaking changes

- `update_weights_from_tensor` and `update_weights_from_distributed` must run inside `begin_weight_update()` ... `end_weight_update()`; callers without a session get `success=False` and a message naming the call to make. Migration is the three-line pattern in the doc section.
- `UpdateWeightsFromTensorReqInput.disable_draft_model` is removed; use `selector="target"`.
- `ChecksumInfo.parallelism_info` is now a list, one entry per role.

## Testing

Lint via pre-commit (Python hooks clean on all files).

- Unit (CPU): `test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_default_model_loader.py` (`postprocess_weights` must not process a LoRA wrapper; fails without the skip), `test/registered/unit/rl/test_distributed_weight_update_spec_worker.py`, `test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_weight_version_tracking.py`, `test/registered/unit/managers/test_msgpack_ipc_roundtrip.py`.
- Unit (1-gpu-small, real kernels): `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_wna16_moe_reload.py` refits a Marlin W4A16 `FusedMoE` (fresh A, refit B, refit A) through `WeightUpdater.begin_weight_update` / `end_weight_update`, the per-runner component the scheduler drives, and requires parameters bitwise equal to fresh loads, unchanged `data_ptr`s, and matching outputs. It is the first caller of `CompressedTensorsWNA16MoE.restore_weights_before_loading` (#15238) on main. Verified on 1x B200: passes on this branch; with the `CompressedTensorsFusedMoEMethod` forwarding removed (main's state) the first refit fails in `_load_w13` with `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (64) must match the size of tensor b (128)`.
- Unit (1-gpu-small, imports only): `test/registered/unit/spec/test_weight_update_runners.py` pins the runners every spec family exposes, including FrozenKV MTP, both DSpark PP positions, multi-layer step roles, NGRAM and UNO.
- E2E: `test_update_weights_from_distributed.py`, `test_update_weights_from_tensor.py`, `test_weight_checker_e2e.py`, `test_utils_update_weights.py`, `test_multi_instance_release_memory_occupation.py`.

Not executed locally: every test above except the Marlin W4A16 refit relies on CI. MXFP8 and NVFP4 finalize correctness is covered by the existing `test_update_weights_from_disk_blackwell.py`, which runs the same `DefaultModelLoader.postprocess_weights` after a full reload. The MoE-LoRA disk-update `AttributeError` on main is inferred from the code and covered by the unit test above, not reproduced end to end. DFlash and DSpark weight updates (all paths) have no e2e coverage; they are exercised only through the enumeration unit test.

title: [MoE] Disable FlashInfer fused finalize by default for numerical accuracy
body:
## Motivation

@humansand

Default to unfused FlashInfer MoE finalize for better numerical accuracy. Users can opt in to fused atomic finalize with `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MOE_FUSED_FINALIZE=1` when they prefer more aggressive performance.

- **History:** [#28354](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28354) introduced this environment variable with `EnvBool(True)` and made deterministic inference force it to `0`.
- **Prior behavior:** immediately before #28354, the [CUTLASS calls](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c4271c3fe1262fc2adbd162c33b25de5255251c5/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py#L221-L238) and [CuTe DSL v2 wrapper](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c4271c3fe1262fc2adbd162c33b25de5255251c5/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutedsl.py#L287-L302) omitted `use_fused_finalize`. SGLang [pinned FlashInfer 0.6.17](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c4271c3fe1262fc2adbd162c33b25de5255251c5/python/pyproject.toml#L36), whose [CUTLASS API](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/a0a6b019b9b27d49d209f85d028a1ae5a9b347d7/flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py#L943) and [CuTe DSL wrapper](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/a0a6b019b9b27d49d209f85d028a1ae5a9b347d7/flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/fused_moe.py#L464) both defaulted to `True`. Thus #28354 exposed the existing fused-finalize default as a SGLang setting; this PR changes that default to `False` for the callers that honor it. The separate CuTe DSL v1 DeepEP masked path is outside this flag's scope.

## Modifications

- **Default:** change `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MOE_FUSED_FINALIZE` from `EnvBool(True)` to `EnvBool(False)`.
- **Documentation:** update the default and explain the performance opt-in.
- **Existing paths:** CUTLASS and CuTe DSL callers continue to read the same flag; deterministic inference continues to force it off. No kernel changes or new tests.

## Accuracy Tests

- **Static validation:** changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed at `e3bcc8f7b4337565baea1d2b44fd4f0f838b1953` (base: `6e1d9c14647e3e16f2a103b89dead95f1400ea48`).
- **Environment:** macOS 26.4.1, arm64, Python 3.14.6, pre-commit 4.6.1; local CPU checks only, no container or GPUs used.
- **Not run:** model accuracy tests; no tests added for this default-only runtime change. Mintlify build/link checks were not run because `mint` is unavailable locally.

The image shipped FlashInfer 0.6.18; all three FlashInfer packages were updated to the matched official post1 release before measurement.
- **Workload:** DeepSeek-V3 MoE: hidden 7,168, intermediate 2,048, 256 experts, top-8, 8 routing groups/top-4 groups, routed scale 2.5, random seed 42, routing bias scale 0.01; simulated EP=8, TP=1: rank 0 holds experts 0–31 of 256. The token count is the global input batch routed across all 256 experts; this single-GPU benchmark computes the local expert contribution. Powers of two from 1 through 16,384 tokens. CUTLASS uses NVFP4 W4A4 per-tensor activation scaling. CuTe DSL covers NVFP4 W4A4 per-tensor, NVFP4 W4A4 per-token, and NVFP4 W4A16 with BF16 input, using its wrapper API.
- **Timing:** one complete flag-True sweep followed by one flag-False sweep for each configuration; no repeated or reverse-order sweeps. Independent autotuning caches per backend/activation/finalize mode; 10 warmups, 100 measured iterations per case, native median GPU latency, CUDA graphs and CUPTI with cold-L2 flushing. Routing, input activation quantization (`--include-activation-quant`, for W4A4), both expert GEMMs, and finalize are included. Weight preparation, compilation, and autotuning are excluded. W4A16 consumes BF16 input directly. All six commands exited 0, yielding all 120 requested latency rows with no CUPTI fallback warnings.
- **Build/provenance:** all EP8 runs used the same physical GPU (UUID `GPU-aa4e94df-96de-22b9-87c2-9960d6b27cb8`), image, and package versions. JIT was left enabled. The release wheel provides `fused_moe_103.so` and `fp4_quantization_103.so` for CUTLASS MoE and FP4 quantization; no CUTLASS build was needed.
- **Limits:** single sweeps provide no repeat/order-variation statistics. This covers local MoE only: no inter-GPU communication, other EP/TP layouts, model accuracy checks, or end-to-end serving. No numerical-error reduction is measured here.

**Speedup = latency with `use_fused_finalize=True` (old default) / latency with `False` (proposed default); greater than 1 means disabling fused finalize is faster.** CUTLASS `True` permits eligible fused-finalize tactics; autotuning can still choose an unfused tactic.

title: fix(moe): Fix per-token quantization `fast-math` INF scale when activation contains all-zero row
body:
## 📌 Description

This PR aims to fix a potential bug in per-token NVFP4 quantization kernel in the `fast-math` path. If the input tensor has a all-zero row, current non `fast-math` path generates 0 scale:
https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/8bc3b578027791336c6ae87db5c9d76f82cef8bc/csrc/nv_internal/tensorrt_llm/kernels/quantization.cuh#L793-L802

But the `fast-math` path will produce INF scale, which ultimately leads to NaN activation. As ReLU2 happens to produce zero rows, this bug causes the accuracy regression in Nemotron-3 series models.

title: Reuse cuDNN attention plans and fix metadata lifetime and layout
body:
## 📌 Description

Repeated cuDNN decode and prefill calls retain compatible prepared graphs and static metadata. Decode query-length storage stays owned by the wrapper across plan/capture/replay; replanning preserves compatible prepared state. Decode sinks bind current values, including copies of strided inputs during capture.

This also repairs adjacent cuDNN attention adapter bugs: paged prefill's default softmax scale, real NHD/HND layouts, packed Stats, and omitted CSR-derived metadata; complete prefill descriptor keys and device identity; FP8 default/scalar scale bindings; and device/thread-local cuDNN handles. Explicitly unsupported masking/scaling features raise instead of being ignored. A shared resolver keeps public and prepared prefill metadata consistent. Shape override declines noncontiguous indptrs. Single-token GQA prefill LSE remains rejected because cuDNN 9.27 leaves heads unwritten (NVBug 6783545).

The public decode API also validates explicitly supplied Q/O offsets. Legacy dense offsets remain accepted, including packed query strides and multi-token decode. Non-dense CUDA offsets trigger a device assertion, including if changed before captured replay. Checks stay on device and are bypassed when offsets are omitted; prepared wrapper execution and cubin offset forwarding are unchanged.

Regression tests include capture -> plan -> allocator poison -> replay, prepared replacement while retaining a capture, changing sinks, descriptor layouts, default scale, O and LSE references, and real replay with poisoned outputs. The legacy BF16 prefill matrix now actually uses its LSE and CUDA-graph parameters. The broad existing FP8 xfail is retained; new targeted FP8 default/scalar tests execute on B200.

Production NVIDIA B200 (148 SMs, 1000 W), BF16, Hq/Hkv=32/8, D=128, NHD. cuDNN 9.27, FE source `d3613cf599831ba74195e714b6c4591334d97761`, DSL 4.8. Both arms use the same native extension SHA256 `40541e6532cb1b7d4082cd05df1724eb850b46c9461e7a3f2f4a536ab6f818e8`. Exact imports and product-file hashes are verified per process.

One plan serves many runs: new Q/K/V values do not require replan while the plan contract remains compatible. Metadata resolution and static descriptor/binding preparation happen in `plan()`. Warm `run()` checks dynamic tensor descriptors and binds current pointers. Same-descriptor replans retain compatible prepared state and stable CPU-metadata device mirrors. Each call owns its variant pack.

**Correction to the earlier ragged GPU comparison:** the old 68.57 us baseline is withdrawn. After capture, the benchmark replanned the original wrapper, releasing GPU metadata still referenced by native graph nodes. The initial replay check passed, but later temporary allocations reused that storage; outputs from the timed loop had 5.8% incorrect elements (maximum absolute error 3.0). Keeping the captured integer metadata references alive restores both correctness and ~71.9 us GPU time. The benchmark now validates outputs after timing as well as before it. No runtime workaround was added for this investigation; the current wrapper already owns stable metadata buffers.

Corrected ABBA comparison below: original runtime `e5faae23` versus current runtime `f12964fb` (unchanged by benchmark/test follow-up `56e95195`). The diagnostic harness retains captured wrapper metadata in **both** arms; this lifetime repair belongs to the benchmark baseline, not the old PR implementation. All four processes pass sampled independent math and full replay checks before and after timing. Median of two process medians, microseconds; ragged prefill B16/Q=KV512:

| Measurement | Original runtime with diagnostic capture retention | Current runtime |
|---|---:|---:|
| Warm host enqueue | 38.52 | 33.76 |
| Run after plan | 47.01 | 44.10 |
| Host plan+run | 88.10 | 100.65 |
| CUDA graph GPU replay | 71.89 | 71.86 |

A separate same-graph/same-buffer experiment interleaves old and new execution with identical tensor pointers, workspace and override arguments: 73.84/73.85 us. Absolute timings differ with that experiment's allocation arrangement; its paired result corroborates GPU parity for this case.

The host plan+run cost remains real. Profiling identifies the complete descriptor and compatibility checks in `_CudnnPrefillPlan.prepare`. A fixed-contract diagnostic bypass reduces current plan+run from 99.36 to 82.06 us while warm enqueue and GPU time stay unchanged. That bypass is **not shipped**: general replans must validate changed descriptors. This PR improves repeated warm execution and preserves capture correctness; it does not claim every-plan-plus-one-run is faster. These are component measurements, not full-model speedups.

Historical decode measurements at `2293b566` remain separate evidence (B64/Q1/KV1024/page16, same FE/native): warm host 34.55 -> 36.32 us; run after plan 67.47 -> 49.61 us; host plan+run 470.48 -> 450.35 us; GPU replay 42.96 -> 42.93 us. They were not remeasured during the ragged attribution.

```bash
python benchmarks/bench_cudnn_wrapper_host.py --kind ragged --batch 16 --q 512 --kv 512 --replan --output ragged.json
```

## 🔍 Related Issues

Follow-up to review of #5350 and adjacent cuDNN integration paths. Most adapter defects predate this PR; the captured decode allocation lifetime and plan-every-step prepared reuse are PR regressions. The v0.7.0 release does not contain #5350, but does contain the older paged-layout/default-scale/Stats, descriptor-key, handle, and FP8-binding defects. This patch targets current main's token-unit wrapper contract; it is not a standalone v0.7.0 backport.

## 🧪 Tests

- [ ] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

**CodeRabbit follow-up (`71c7408d`):** focused decode/cache-key/prepared/wrapper suites pass **170 tests / 1 skipped on SM100** and **160 / 11 on H100**. This includes dense Q/O offset compatibility for packed Q and multi-token decode, capture/replay, metadata contract rejection, and unchanged cubin forwarding. Invalid GPU offsets are tested in isolated subprocesses because a device assertion invalidates that CUDA context. A capture/mutation negative control fails on the previous `56e95195` runtime, which silently ignores the changed offset.

The benchmark now restricts replan-after-capture to cuDNN while continuing to measure eager plan+run for other backends. FA2 and cuDNN pass both decode and ragged `--replan` smoke runs, cross-backend output checks and the post-timing replay gate. JSON retains all raw timing samples, imported package version, checkout commit and source dirty state. Changed-file pre-commit, including mypy and Ruff, passes.

Prepared wrapper and graph execution source is unchanged. H100 ABBA decode (B64/Q1/KV1024/page16, same FE/native) measures warm host 40.41 -> 40.44 us and GPU replay 93.62 -> 93.51 us. Ragged GPU replay differs by less than 0.04%; host measurements are noisy and reverse direction between repetitions, so those samples establish no ragged host speedup/regression. Explicit offsets in the low-level API add device validation work; ordinary prepared wrapper execution does not pay that cost. This follow-up has no new B200 measurement.

**Benchmark/test follow-up (`56e95195`):** the benchmark refuses timings if the final timed output fails its full one-ULP replay gate. The old baseline fails this new guard; current code passes on B200. Ragged direct and forced-legacy tests now capture O/LSE, replan with new CPU metadata tensors, poison the allocator with integer buffers, and check replay against independent math. The regression file passes **43 tests / 1 skipped on production B200**, **43 / 1 on the SM100 development GPU**, and **37 / 7 on H100**. Changed-file pre-commit passed. Production files are unchanged from `f12964fb`.

**Cleanup (`f12964fb`):** removes unused matcher/cache/decode forwarding state and redundant paged KV staging while retaining public signatures and plan-owned caches. Production growth versus the PR base is +991 lines. Focused contract/prepared/wrapper suites: **76 passed / 1 skipped on SM100**, **70 / 7 on H100**; another **23 H100 public decode/cache-key tests** passed. The public fallback probe counted 19 nonprepared plans and 19 fallback launches. Capability absence was simulated by patching both wrapper and low-level aliases on the current installation, rather than claiming tests on an older FE release.

FP8 default/scalar/tensor capture coverage, caller-owned metadata protection, descriptor/layout changes, current pointer rebinding, NHD/HND, packed O/LSE and workspace replacement remain covered. title: fix(moe): write fused-shared routing replay as routed-only [T, K]
body:
## 📌 Description

Fixes #5009 part 1. DeepSeek `routingMainKernel` wrote `routing_replay_out` with the packed index `token * (K+S) + k`. Replay is `[T, K]` (routed ids only), so token 1 starts at `K+S` instead of `K`. `S == 0` hid it; host/C++ rejected `S > 0` (#4239), so the combo was unavailable.

This PR indexes replay with `token * K + k` and drops the `S > 0` rejects. Packed ids/weights stay `[T, K+S]`.

title: Assert cached decode matches recomputing without a cache
body:
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48289&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48289) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48289&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48289)


Claude flagged this while i was doing some work on exporters.

`GenerationTesterMixin` already ran greedy generate with and without a cache, but each test only checked its own shapes — nothing compared them, so a cache that feeds its layers the wrong positions or a mask of the wrong width passed both. Driving each side through `generate` keeps the modality, encoder-decoder and input-naming plumbing in the library, which is what lets one assertion cover text, VLM and encoder-decoder models alike.

It compares per-step logits, then ids up to the first near-tie — tie-checking the scores rather than the logits, since the ids are picked after the processors run and `min_new_tokens` drives EOS to -inf. Models whose state *is* their cache skip on `_is_stateful`.

Across every model it found four real bugs:

- fsmt embedded positions from the sliced one-token input, so every decode step re-read position `padding_idx + 1`. On real weights the drift flips a token by step 6; an earlier commit had overwritten the expected en-ru translation to absorb it, and the fix restores the original text for all four pairs.
- axk2, deepseek_v32 and glm_moe_dsa fold their sparse top-k into the attention mask with `masked_fill`, which writes True — i.e. *attend* — when the mask is boolean, as it is on the sdpa path. Padded sequences longer than `index_topk` attended future tokens.
- paligemma (and v1) let generated tokens inherit the prompt's `token_type_ids`, putting them in the bidirectionally-attending prefix block, so without a cache earlier tokens attended tokens generated after them.
- vibevoice_asr dropped its audio inputs after prefill even with no cache, so the placeholders fell back to text embeddings.

blt (decode rebuilds hash n-grams and patch lengths from one byte and gives the global trunk no cache), vibevoice_asr's residual VAE sampling and prophetnet's collapsed single-step branch are skipped with the measured mechanism.

Fixes # (issue)

title: Fix Qwen2.5-VL temporal RoPE for fractional video intervals
body:
[![CPU CI](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48669&event=pr-ci)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48669) [![GPU run-slow](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/badge/pr?pr=48669&event=run-slow)](https://transformers-ci.lor-e.huggingface.cool/d/pytest-observability-by-pr/pytest-observability-branch?var-pr=48669)


# What does this PR do?

Fixes premature truncation of fractional video timing in Qwen2.5-VL temporal RoPE.

`get_rope_index` currently converts each `second_per_grid_ts` value to an integer before multiplying by `tokens_per_second`. With a temporal patch size of 2 and an effective sampling rate of 4 FPS, the interval is 0.5 seconds and is truncated to zero. All temporal grids in that video consequently receive the same temporal coordinate. Non-integral intervals above one second also lose their fractional component.

Keep the temporal step floating point and convert the complete per-grid temporal coordinates to `long` in `get_vision_position_ids`. For `tokens_per_second=2`, four grids with 0.5-second intervals now have relative temporal coordinates `[0, 1, 2, 3]` instead of `[0, 0, 0, 0]`. Quantization happens after multiplying by the grid index, so fractional scaled steps such as 1.5 also accumulate correctly.

The Qwen2.5-VL modular source overrides its inherited vision-position helper to keep this behavior change local to Qwen2.5-VL. The generated modeling file is regenerated with the repository converter. Image coordinates and integer-interval behavior are preserved.

This restores the quantization order used by the earlier implementation:
- [Transformers v4.49.0](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v4.49.0/src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py#L1533-L1538)
- [Qwen's public fine-tuning implementation](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen2.5-VL/blob/main/qwen-vl-finetune/qwenvl/data/rope2d.py#L248-L253)

## Validation

- Regression covers 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 and 1.5 seconds, with Python-list and tensor inputs; checks temporal/spatial coordinates, output dtype, and RoPE deltas.
- Running the regression with the two original methods from baseline `4815a0a` produces 8 failing fractional-interval subtests; both integer-interval subtests pass.
- With this change: 10 regression subtests pass, alongside the existing `test_vision_position_ids` and `test_video_forward` tests.
- Ruff lint and format checks pass for all three changed files.
- Modular conversion consistency check passes for Qwen2.5-VL.
- Tested on CPU; no full accelerator suite or downstream accuracy evaluation was run.

Commands (with the checkout's `src` on `PYTHONPATH`):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/models/qwen2_5_vl/test_modeling_qwen2_5_vl.py -k 'vision_position_ids or video_position_ids_fractional_seconds or test_video_forward' -q
python utils/check_modular_conversion.py --files src/transformers/models/qwen2_5_vl/modular_qwen2_5_vl.py --check_all --num_workers 1
```

title: [Feat][Core/Auth] Enable token authentication for local clusters by default
body:
## Description

Enable token authentication for local clusters by default.

The table below shows the resulting behavior. Remote and worker paths are unchanged.

| Entry point | `RAY_AUTH_MODE` unset, token exists | `RAY_AUTH_MODE` unset, no token | `RAY_AUTH_MODE=token` | `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`ray.init()`** (new local cluster, no address) | enable + **reuse** token + **warn** | enable + **generate** token + **warn** | enable (generate/reuse), no warning | disabled, no warning |
| **`ray start --head`** (local head) | enable + reuse token + **warn** | disabled + **warn** | enable; **raises** if no token, no warning | disabled, no warning |
| **`ray.init(address=…)`** (connect to existing) | unchanged, no auto-enable; needs token if cluster requires it | unchanged | requires token, else error | disabled |
| **`ray start --address=…`** (worker) | unchanged, no auto-enable | unchanged | requires token, else error | disabled |

A token "exists" if any of these resolve, checked in order:

1. `RAY_AUTH_TOKEN` environment variable
2. file at `RAY_AUTH_TOKEN_PATH`
3. default file `~/.ray/auth_token`

## Related issues
N/A

## Additional information

To enable this for all clusters in the future:

- Change the default to "token" here: https://github.com/ray-project/ray/blob/1439e47b9b136143fbc99417cb4f50a82eff72a9/src/ray/common/ray_config_def.h#L39. That is the single source of truth, and `RAY_AUTH_MODE=disabled` stays as the opt-out.
- Remove the auto-enable helper functions from this PR (`enable_token_auth_by_default`, `maybe_enable_token_auth_if_token_available`) and their call sites in `worker.py` and `scripts.py`.
- Decide whether `ray start --head` should auto-generate a token instead of erroring. The worker and connect paths would then require a distributed token, which is a breaking change.
- The cluster launcher, KubeRay, and autoscaler would need to distribute the token to workers automatically. Test fixtures would need to provision a token, and every client path would need to attach it.
- Update `token-auth.md` and the guides that say "disabled by default".

title: [core] Tombstone lease ids on CancelWorkerLease
body:
Following up on #56195 and making CancelWorkerLease truly idempotent by tombstoning lease ids. There's currently a race with RequestWorkerLease where if the RequestWorkerLease RPC arrives AFTER CancelWorkerLease RPC then we just repeatedly trigger additional CancelWorkerLease RPC requests. We've seen a couple cases where there's a large amount of CancelWorkerLease RPC requests and this PR roughly bounds the number of CancelWorkerLease RPCs to O(number of leases), and this should allow us to ignore the message reordering case completely. 

There is still one potential race on the other side where if for some reason the lease is granted from the perspective of the raylet, but the reply takes a while to reach the core worker for some reason, the core worker could potentially spam additional CancelWorkerLease requests for the same lease id. Leaving this as a follow up to verify if it actually matters.

title: [Serve] Configurable status code and Retry-After header for backpressure rejections
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

When a request is rejected due to backpressure (`max_queued_requests` exceeded), Serve returns HTTP `503` — the same status code returned when a deployment is unavailable (e.g., it failed to deploy). Clients and infrastructure can't distinguish "deliberate load shedding, retry shortly" from "the service is broken":

- 5xx from load shedding burns availability SLOs and pages on-call for a system that's working as designed (shedding to protect latency).
- Envoy/GCP LB outlier detection ejects backends on consecutive 5xx; a pod shedding load can get ejected, concentrating traffic on the remaining pods. 429 never triggers ejection.
- `retry_on: 5xx` policies blindly re-execute shed requests; a 429 is only retried when explicitly configured.

The gRPC path already makes this exact distinction: since #54537, `BackPressureError` maps to `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (the gRPC analog of HTTP 429) while `DeploymentUnavailableError` maps to `UNAVAILABLE`. This PR brings the HTTP path to parity, opt-in, with a new per-deployment `backpressure_config` option (`serve.config.BackpressureConfig`, following the `autoscaling_config` / `request_router_config` pattern):

```python
from ray.serve.config import BackpressureConfig

@serve.deployment(
    max_ongoing_requests=32,
    max_queued_requests=64,
    backpressure_config=BackpressureConfig(   # also accepts a plain dict / YAML mapping
        status_code=429,                      # 503 (default) or 429
        retry_after_s=5,                      # attach "Retry-After: 5"; None (default) = no header
    ),
)
```

- `status_code`: status code for backpressure rejections only. `DeploymentUnavailableError` responses always remain 503. Restricted to {503, 429}.
- `retry_after_s`: attaches a `Retry-After` header (RFC 9110 delay-seconds, rounded up) to backpressure rejections. Orthogonal to the status code — RFC 9110 defines Retry-After for 503, and RFC 6585 allows it on 429, so it can be enabled with either. OpenAI/Anthropic-style SDKs honor Retry-After (≤60s) on both status codes.

Defaults preserve today's behavior exactly (503, no header) for backward compatibility with existing dashboards, alerts, and the documented 503 contract.

## Implementation

- New public `serve.config.BackpressureConfig` model with fields typed `Literal[503, 429]` and `Optional[NonNegativeFloat]` (`allow_inf_nan=False`) so the constraints are enforced statically and export into the generated JSON schema (`"enum": [503, 429]`, `"minimum": 0`) used by the declarative REST config API — no custom validators needed. `DeploymentConfig` holds it via `default_factory` with `NeedsActorReconfigure` so runtime updates reach the replica-local config the direct-ingress path reads; the details API returns the full stable dict shape via `model_dump()` (same as `autoscaling_config`). Carried in `serve.proto` as a nested `BackpressureConfig` message (field 24) with presence-tracked members so configs from older controllers during rolling upgrades fall back to defaults.
- `BackPressureError` carries `status_code` / `retry_after_s` from the raise site in the router (which has the deployment config). All constructor args are passed to `Exception.__init__` so they survive pickling across process boundaries (cf. #50211).
- The HTTP proxy's `get_http_response_status()` reads the fields off the exception; `ResponseStatus` gains an optional `headers` field (HTTP path only; gRPC ignores it).
- Direct-ingress HTTP rejection (`replica.py`) and the FastAPI exception handler for uncaught `BackPressureError` from downstream handles use the same config/fields.
- gRPC behavior is unchanged (`RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, no headers).

## Testing

- Unit tests: config validation (incl. dict coercion and inf/nan rejection), proto round-trip (explicit values, defaults, old-proto fallback), HTTP status mapping with and without headers, Retry-After delay-seconds rounding and clamping, `send_http_response_on_exception` incl. 429, `BackPressureError` pickle round-trip, old-style 2-arg construction, `requires_actor_reconfigure` coverage.
- The three HTTP tests in `tests/test_backpressure.py` are parametrized over the default (503, no header) and configured (429, `Retry-After: 7`) responses, covering the proxy, model-composition, and FastAPI-composition paths.
- E2E smoke-tested on a local cluster (classic proxy path and `RAY_SERVE_ENABLE_DIRECT_INGRESS=1`): flooding a `max_ongoing_requests=1, max_queued_requests=1` deployment yields `[200, 200, 429×6]` with `Retry-After: 7` when configured, and `[200, 200, 503×6]` with no header by default.
